newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin has long record of health problems.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin has long record of health problems.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin was admitted to hospital on Wednesday with what the Kremlin said was the first signs of pneumonia.
The quick announcement of his transfer to the Central Clinical Hospital in Moscow was in stark contrast with the former Kremlin tradition of secrecy over the state of health of the country's leaders.
Until last September, when Yeltsin announced his decision to have a heart operation, he and his aides had denied he had any serious worries.
Following is a chronology of his health problems.

1949-1955 - Yeltsin plays volleyball for several hours a day and studies at night. The stress lands him in hospital, but he ignores doctors' warnings and discharges himself. "The risk was colossal and I could have ruined my heart forever," he says in his autobiography.

Nov 9, 1987 - Yeltsin is taken to hospital with head and heart pains after being humiliated by the communist leadership. He is treated with sedatives for nervous stress and describes his headache at the time as the "torture of hell".
1990 - Yeltsin's plane crash lands in Spain and Barcelona. Doctors operate on his back.
Oct 1991 - Yeltsin is ordered to take two weeks' rest after aides say he suffered minor heart problems.
Jan 1992 - Yeltsin fails to meet Japan's foreign minister. Tokyo news agencies quote aides saying he has a heart condition but he reappears in good spirits 24 hours later.
Feb 1992 - Yeltsin tells French television: "I have never had any heart trouble. Every day I have a cold shower -- I am in very good shape."
April 1992 - Yeltsin misses a meeting with then U.S. treasury secretary Nicholas Brady. He said he was working, the media said he was drunk.
April 1993 - He says: "I have only two problems -- tiredness and lack of sleep. There are no other health problems."
Sept 1993 - Yeltsin, suffering back pains, invites the Spanish surgeon who operated on him in 1990 to Moscow.
April 1994 - Yeltsin offers to undergo a public check-up "to show everything I have inside me, from blood to urine". He adds: "I hope you will all be as well as I am when you reach my age."
Dec 1994 - Yeltsin has a minor operation on his nose and disappears from the public eye, officially due to this, while thousands of Russian troops roll into rebel Chechnya.
April 1995 - Yeltsin's spokesman says he suffers from high blood pressure which can cause sporadic muscle weakness.
July 1995 - Yeltsin goes into hospital with an ischaemic heart condition -- a blood supply problem. He spends two weeks in hospital followed by two weeks in a sanatorium.
Oct 26, 1995 - Yeltsin again suffers from ischaemia. He spends over two months in hospital and in a sanatorium, leaving on New Year's Eve.
Feb 1996 - Yeltsin launches a vigorous campaign to win a second term in office. He travels non-stop, holds dozens of meetings, dances the twist and swings on a swing.
June 28, 1996 - Yeltsin disappears from public view a week before the end of the campaign. Aides say he has a sore throat. He has never really returned to the public eye since then.
July 3, 1996 - Yeltsin fails to vote at his regular Moscow polling station as scheduled and votes at the Barvikha residence which also houses a medical centre.
Aug 2, 1996 - A Yeltsin aide says the president is suffering from "colossal weariness" after his election campaign and needs two months of peace and quiet.
Aug 19, 1996 - The Kremlin denies a Time magazine report that Yeltsin would go to a Swiss clinic for a bypass operation.
Sept 5, 1996 - Yeltsin, breaking with Kremlin tradition, says he will have heart surgery. He says he expects the operation to be in Moscow at the end of the month.

Sept 13, 1996 - Yeltsin goes into Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital for what aides say will be a weekend of pre-surgical tests. The stay is extended several times and Yeltsin leaves hospital only in early October, moving back to Barvikha.

Sept 20, 1996 - Surgeon Renat Akchurin, expected to lead the operation on Yeltsin, tells a U.S. television channel Yeltsin had an unreported heart attack in late June or early July. Yeltsin aides later play down the report.
Sept 25, 1996 - Yeltsin's medical team says it will take six to 10 weeks to prepare the president for surgery.
Oct 9, 1996 - Pioneering U.S. surgeon Michael DeBakey, who will advise Russian doctors on the operation, says he expects Yeltsin to make a full recovery.

Nov 5, 1996 - Yeltsin has quintuple bypass operation. Doctors say the operation went well and Yeltsin recovers quickly, first at the Cardiology Centre, then at the central Clinical Hospital and then at several country residences.
December 23, 1996 - Yeltsin, returning to work in the Kremlin, promises to be an "active and energetic president".
Since his return to the Kremlin, Yeltsin maintains a busy schedule, including talks with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on January 4 during which Yeltsin looked pale and moved stiffly.
January 6, 1997 - Yeltsin cancels all meetings and the Kremlin says he has a "heavy cold".
January 8, 1997 - Yeltsin is admitted to the Central Clinical hospital in Moscow with what the Kremlin describes as first signs of pneumonia.
